uncited: *   **Input:** Volumetric dataset, importance values $I_o$ for each object/region, camera parameters (view direction, projection type), and a depth buffer containing the "last-hit" depth for each pixel.
*   **Output:** A 2D image where the highest-importance object is visible, and occluding lower-importance objects are removed.
*   **Depth Footprint:** A 2D image (same resolution as the output) where each pixel $i$ stores the depth $z_i$ of the last sample of the highest-importance object along the corresponding ray.
*   **Distance Field:** A 2D image derived from the depth footprint, storing the distance $d_i$ of each pixel from the footprint boundary, computed via a 2D chamfer distance transform.
*   **Gradient Field:** A 3D vector field (or modified gradient values) used to simulate the lighting of the cut-away surface.
**Identify Focus Object:** For each ray, determine the object with the maximum importance value $I_{max}$.
**Generate Depth Footprint:** Render the volume to determine the depth of the last-hit sample for the focus object at each pixel.
**Compute Distance Field:** Apply a 2D chamfer distance transform to the depth footprint.
*   **Time Complexity:** The method requires an initial pass to compute the depth footprint and distance field ($O(N)$ for $N$ pixels), followed by the main raycasting pass.
Maximum Importance Projection (MImP) was introduced as part of Importance-Driven Volume Rendering.
